title: Vector Physics MCQ — Page 55 (Q1–Q2)
notes:
**Q1. Which of the following is a scalar quantity?**

(a) Force
(b) Magnetic field
(c) Electric potential
(d) Magnetic moment

**Answer:** (c) Electric potential

**Explanation:** Electric potential is defined as work done per unit charge ($W/q$). Since both work and charge are scalar quantities, electric potential has only magnitude and no directional dependencies.

**Q2. Which of the following is a vector quantity?**

(a) Temperature
(b) Electric current
(c) Pressure
(d) Weight

**Answer:** (d) Weight

**Explanation:** Weight is a gravitational pull acting on a mass. It possesses both magnitude and a distinct, downward spatial vector direction targeting the center of gravity.
